issues.legal_issue: An accused who intentionally inflicts the injuries actually suffered by the victim is guilty of murder when those injuries are sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, even without an intention to cause death.
material_facts: Two eyewitnesses gave trustworthy accounts that the accused attacked the victim and inflicted injuries on him.
One accused struck the victim on the head, causing fractures to both parietal bones.
The medical evidence established that the head injuries were grievous and sufficient to cause death.
The trial court found that the accused had intended the injuries inflicted, although it found no intention to cause death.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the accused were guilty of murder, upheld the High Court’s alteration of their convictions to murder, and dismissed their appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause thirdly of Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code, murder is established where the accused intended to inflict the particular injuries actually caused and those injuries were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death; an intention to cause death is not necessary. The court relied on Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab, 1958 SCR 1985, and State of Andhra Pradesh v. Royavarasu Punnayya, and held the offence punishable under Section 302 of the Code.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_murder_conviction and eyewitness_evidence_reliable and accused_intended_actual_injuries and injuries_sufficient_to_cause_death

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_murder_convictio: The proceeding is an appeal by accused convicted of murder.
predicates.eyewitness_evidence_reliable: Eyewitnesses gave accounts of the accused inflicting injuries on the victim that the court found trustworthy.
predicates.accused_intended_actual_injuries: The accused intended to inflict the particular injuries that the victim actually suffered.
predicates.injuries_sufficient_to_cause_death: The injuries inflicted were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.

issues.definition: When a murder-conviction appeal concerns reliable evidence that the accused intended the actual injuries inflicted and those injuries were sufficient to cause death, the rule treats the accused as guilty of murder.
